tspan.tspan: Background
Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has seen many
improvements in recent years, one of which is an
increase in spatial resolution which has led to the
need for better tools for data visualisation and data
analysis [1]. The use of autoencoders as a method to
compress MSI data was first introduced by Thomas
et al. [2]. This only allowed for learning a discrete
non-regularised latent space, and therefore in order
to
make use of a model with generative properties, a
variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture was
employed.
Method
The MSI data was passed through different
variations
of a variational autoencoder. The latent
spaces that
were learnt were clustered using K-
means clustering.
The latent spaces were visualised
using UMAP and t-
SNE. The clusters were
overalayed on these plots.
The spatial distribution of
the clusters were also
evaluated in order to link any
learnt representations
to observations in the tissue
that was imaged.
Data Description
The training data for the VAE was made up of 160
000 spectra that were captured in a 400 by 400 grid.
Each spectra consisted of intensity readings at
different mass-to-charge values. The intensity
readings were binned uniformly into 70 000 bins.
This is why the VAE input took in 70 000 values.
The cluster centroids obtained by running K-Means
on the latent space were passed through the decoder
of the VAE and the produced spectra are shown
below. The spectra look extremely similar but when
the MSE was measured between the output,
differences were noted. The figure on the right
shows the spatial representation of different intensity
values across spectra at a specific mass-to-charge
value.

text.tspan: Due to the latent space representing very similar
spectra, the average and maximum values for the
different bin indices were recorded across all of the
spectra and are plotted below. It is important to note
that the mean spectrum is very similar to the spectra
that were being represented in the latent space.
Out of the 12 clusters learnt, few showed potential at representing
meaningul information in the spatial domain. Cluster 7 highlights
that some of the latent space was able to capture meaningful
information.
